author: ValWood
body:
I'm filtering this annotation

GO:0032267 | tRNA(Ile)-lysidine synthase activity | IEA with 43744

Although it looks like a  tRNA(Ile)-lysidine synthase activity this seems highly unlikely because TilS specifically acts on tRNA isoleucine with a CAU anticodon, which pombe doesn't have

author: marcfeuermann
body:
I just looked at the corresponding entry. It is a very old one which has not been touched since at least 20 years. It seems that the function has been accepted and propagated since decades.
I general, the sequence is not very conserved.
Moreover, I've checked for specific publications for S. pombe til1 and did not find any.

My new best friend ChatGPT agrees:
'There do not appear to be any papers that experimentally characterise til1 (SPAC12B10.08c) specifically in Schizosaccharomyces pombe. The gene is annotated in PomBase/UniProt as the mitochondrial tRNA(Ile)-lysidine synthase (Til1), but that functional assignment is inferred from homology to well-studied bacterial TilS enzymes rather than from a dedicated S. pombe paper.'

So we have no idea about what it is doing...
I am not a magician, but what I could propose is to change its name to 'tRNA(Ile)-lysidine synthase-like protein' and remove any annotations related to the catalytic activity.
I would also add a caution comment stating that S. pombe does not have the CAU codon.
This should solve the problem.
Let me know if it is okay for you.
Thanks,
Marc.

author: ValWood
body:
That is EXACTLY what I did at PomBase

tRNA(Ile)-lysidine synthase-like protein'
and
a comment
misc, TilS specifically acts on tRNA isoleucine with a CAU anticodon, which S. pombe does not have

 the plant and plasmodium members appear to be OK, there seems to be evidence that plastid genomes have this activity, so  the yeast appear to be outliers
